grade.first_issue: In Step 3, the assertion that for every n one can choose m∈N with |z+nC-(w+mD)|≤D is false. For example, even for the valid solution f(t)=t+1, taking z=2, w=100, and n=0 makes this impossible. This approximation is load-bearing for proving equality of the positive defect values, so Rule C applies.
grade.summary: The claimed classification f(x)=x+c, c≥0, is correct, and nearly all of the proof—including orbit invariance, nonnegativity of c, the range estimate, the connectedness argument, and verification—is sound. The false quantifier in the orbit-approximation step prevents the proof from being complete as submitted. It is repaired directly by restricting to all sufficiently large n (so z+nC≥w) and taking m=floor((z+nC-w)/D), which gives distance less than D. Because the false statement is load-bearing, Rule C caps the score at 5.
strengths: Correctly obtains f^n(x)=x+nc(x) and hence c(x)≥0.
Derives a valid quadratic bound for differences of c on Im(f).
The mixed-value exclusion via two relatively open sets is correct.
Correctly verifies every translation f(x)=x+c with c≥0.

errors.description: The lattice-approximation claim is stated for every n, although it is only true for sufficiently large n when m is required to be a natural number. This false assertion supplies the central comparison of positive defect values; its correction is routine but load-bearing.
